whatTheyArgued: Everyday social life is dramaturgical: people manage the impression others form (front stage), and keep a back region where the performance is dropped; teams protect the performance. Stigma (1963) separately treats information control and concealment of discrediting facts. Neither is a theory of PII, data protection, or detection tools.

scholarship.supports: front/back stage, impression management; Stigma on concealing discrediting information
scholarship.disputes: critics argue dramaturgy is cynical/instrumental about the self; not examined further here

ourUse: goffman.js detects HIPAA/GDPR/PCI identifier shapes and reports category, location, count, never the value.

bends.ours: credit line: 'a person's identifying particulars belong to their own performance; a detector that prints them is itself a leak (1959)'.
bends.theirs: 1959 book argues nothing about identifying particulars belonging to the performer, or about detectors; the 'detector that prints PII is a leak' rule is OUR design law, put in the credit field in Goffman's voice.

bends.ours: Identifiers as owned particulars of a person (a privacy/ownership frame).
bends.theirs: For Goffman the self-presentation is a managed impression to an audience, a social accomplishment; he is not making a claim about personal data ownership. Closest real material is Stigma on information control, which the organ does not cite.

bends.ours: Handle: Goffman on an organ whose shapes are derived wholly from HIPAA, GDPR, CCPA, PCI-DSS.
bends.theirs: None of its logic comes from Goffman; the legal instruments do all the work, so the name is a label.
